features.optics-sfp-plus: 10 GbE SFP+ transceivers and direct attach copper cables
features.ptp: the GM/PTP grandmaster clock port; support is not available in the release the guide covers

management.usb: one USB port for installing Junos OS

performance.sfp-plus-speeds: 10 GbE on each of the eight SFP+ ports
performance.switching-capacity: up to 400 Gbps throughput (guide, EX9251 Switch Hardware Overview); the datasheet says up to 800 Gbps
performance.wire-speed-density: 24 x 10 GbE, 4 x 40 GbE or 4 x 100 GbE at wire speed (datasheet, Table 4)

physical.depth-note: 18.5 in (47 cm), or 20.43 in (51.89 cm) with the fan tray and power supply handles (guide Table 4)
physical.weight-note: 22.7 lb (10.3 kg) chassis, with the power supplies and fan trays installed (guide Table 4); the datasheet says 23.15 lb (10.5 kg) fully loaded
physical.width-note: 19 in (48.26 cm) with the brackets in the guide, 17.6 in (44.7 cm) in the datasheet; the body is modelled

power.power-datasheet-max-w: 300 W on AC and 312 W on DC (datasheet Table 3)
power.power-envelope-note: fully loaded switch; 240 W typical at 25 C, 280 W maximum at 55 C (guide Table 12)
power.power-input-ac: 100 to 240 VAC, 50 to 60 Hz; 3.2 A at 100 VAC, 1.37 A at 240 VAC; system input power 312 W
power.power-input-dc: operating -44 to -72 VDC, nominal -48 and -60 VDC; 20 A at -44 VDC maximum; system input power 331 W

thermal.fans: three fan trays, each with one counter-rotating fan, and a fan in each supply

ac.description: EX9251-8X4C: the chassis with two AC power supplies (the guide's Table 2 calls them AC AFO 650W PSU) and three fan trays (JNP-FAN-1RU), with the blank panels the datasheet says ship with it. Front-to-back airflow.

base.description: The switch as it ships with AC power: two AC power supplies and three fan trays in, no slot left empty. The EX9251 has no traffic slots, so the base is the AC order below without its part number.

chas.description: EX9251-CHAS, the spare chassis (guide Table 3). It is listed as a spare part; the guide does not say what it ships with, so the bays are shown open, with no supplies and no fan trays. The blank panel JNP-PWR-BLNK-1 is a separate spare.

dc.description: EX9251-8X4C-DC: the chassis with two DC power supplies (JPSU-650W-DC-AFO) and three fan trays (JNP-FAN-1RU). Front-to-back airflow.

single-psu.description: The EX9251-8X4C with one supply and the blank panel JNP-PWR-BLNK-1 over slot 1, as the guide allows ("a single power supply provides the maximum configuration"). An illustration, not an order code.

datasheet.title: Juniper EX9250 Ethernet Switch Datasheet (1000632-006-EN, Sep 2021)

description: Juniper EX9251, a 1RU fixed-configuration core and aggregation switch that runs Junos OS, the smaller of the two EX9250 chassis. The front has 8 SFP+ ports (10 GbE) in two rows of four, 4 rate-selectable QSFP28 ports (100, 40 or 10 GbE), a GM/PTP SFP cage, a MGMT RJ-45, and the timing and service ports: BITS, CON (console), ToD, a USB port, and 1PPS and 10MHz SMB connectors in and out. The rear carries three fan trays, two power supply slots and the grounding points. The Routing Engine is built in. One panel serves three orders: the AC model, the DC model and the spare chassis.

gaps.note: Width: the guide's Table 4 says 19 in (48.26 cm), which is with the brackets; the datasheet says 17.6 in (44.7 cm) and the specifications page 17.4 in (44.2 cm). Height: 1.72 in (43.7 mm), 1.75 in (44.5 mm) and 1.75 in (44.4 mm). Depth: 18.5 in (469.9 mm), 18.7 in (475 mm) and 18 in (457 mm). The datasheet's width, the guide's height and the guide's depth are carried.
gaps.wanted: a mechanical drawing of the chassis, or Juniper's confirmation of the body width, height and depth
The part numbers of the front-mounting brackets, rear-mounting brackets and ETSI brackets, which the guide lists by name only, and the bracket extents. They are in the accessory box.

A photograph of an EX9251 power supply. The two supplies are juniper/ex4600-jpsu-650-ac-afo@1 and -dc-afo@1, which carry the EX4600's size (54.7 x 40.5 mm) and an orange handle; the EX9251 guide's Table 4 gives the supplies 56.6 mm wide and 40.1 mm (AC) or 42.4 mm (DC) high, and says nothing about a handle colour. The AC supply's part number is not printed in the guide ("AC AFO 650W PSU"); the datasheet's spare number is JNP-PWR650-AC.
The colour of the fan tray handle. The guide draws the tray as a line drawing and states no colour or airflow code; the tray is drawn dark grey with the label AIR OUT.
Where the ToD port's lamp is. The guide says "the LEDs for the ToD port" are lit steadily green but its Table 7 lists none and Figure 1 draws none; the BITS jack has two lamps in the top corners.
the GM/PTP port's behaviour; the guide says support for the port is not available in this release

The rate of the GM/PTP SFP cage and the optic it takes. The guide says only that it connects the switch to a timing device, and that support for it is not available in this release. Searched the guide for GM/PTP: Figure 1 callout 16, Figure 48 callout 1, and no table. The cage is typed sfp-ptp so that it claims no rate.

What the BITS jack carries, a T1, an E1 or another clock signal. The guide calls it the building-integrated timing supply clock interface (Table 37) and gives no rate or framing. Searched the guide for BITS and for T1: Tables 7, 36 and 37 and the connection procedure only. The jack is typed rj48, as the library types every BITS jack, which is a classification and not a reading of this guide.
The USB revision. The guide says Junos supports USB version 1.0 and later and that the flash drives must be USB 2.0 or later; the port is drawn with the neutral usb2 skin.
Table 25 lists a mini-USB Type-B console port among the management cables, which Figure 1 does not show; the front panel has the RJ-45 CON only, and no mini-USB console is drawn.

A straight-on photograph of the front and of the rear. The photograph held is a three-quarter view of the front, so no position was measured off it; every position comes from the guide's flat figures.

The Junos names of the ports. The guide's Table 2 names the PICs (4XQSFP28 in slot 0, 8XSFPP in slot 1) and refers the reader to the Hardware Compatibility Tool for transceivers; it prints no interface name.
The depth of the supplies and fan trays is in Table 4 (14.5 in and 5.78 in) and is not drawn; no component states a depth.

buttons.description: The OFFLINE button and the recessed RESET button (guide Figure 1, callouts 8 and 9)

esd.description: the wrist-strap ESD point at the lower left of the front, and the one at the rear

fan-leds.description: The status lamp in the strip at the left of each fan slot, bicolour: green when the tray is running, red when it is faulty (guide Figure 12, Table 8)

attrs.redundancy-note: Guide, Component Redundancy lists the cooling system among the redundant components: the switch supports three fan trays and, when one fan fails, "the speed of the remaining fans is automatically adjusted". The guide gives no N+M form of its own, so N is the three less one

grounding.description: the protective earthing terminal at the left of the rear, two tapped holes for 10-32 screws 16 mm apart (guide, Grounding Points Specifications)

labels.description: the laser hazard mark beside the SFP+ block (guide Figure 1)

mgmt.mixed: the management cluster at the front: an RJ-45 management Ethernet port, an RJ-45 serial console and a USB port. Three kinds, one purpose: reaching and recovering the switch when the data plane cannot.

attrs.redundancy-note: Two supplies, slots 0 and 1; one supply carries the maximum configuration and the second is for 1+1 feed redundancy. Do not mix AC and DC supplies

qsfp28.description: Ports 0/0 to 0/3 as printed. Each runs as one 100 GbE or 40 GbE port, or as 4 x 10 GbE with a breakout cable

qsfp28-leds.description: The four lamps above each QSFP28 cage, LED0 to LED3 (guide Figure 4, Table 5): LED0 is the 100G or 40G link and the first 10G lane, LED1 to LED3 the other 10G lanes

sfp-plus.description: Ports 1/0 to 1/7 as printed, in four columns of two; the upper cage of a column is even

sfp-plus-leds.description: The lamp of each SFP+ port, a triangle in the band between the rows (guide Figures 5 and 6, Table 6)

status-leds.description: The chassis lamps OK/FAIL, ONLINE, ALM, SSD1 and SSD0 (guide Table 7)

timing.mixed: the timing ports at the front: the GM/PTP SFP cage, the BITS and ToD RJ-45 jacks and the 10MHz and 1PPS SMB connectors, in and out. Three kinds of connector, one purpose: taking a clock or time reference in and giving one out.

timing-leds.description: The two lamps in the top corners of the BITS jack, activity at the left and link at the right (guide Figure 8, Table 7)

name: ex9251

airflow.note: The guide: the switch has front-to-back (AIR OUT) airflow, intake through the front vents and exhaust at the rear, and the datasheet says front-to-back for both models. There is no back-to-front build, so no airflow configuration is written.

buttons.note: Figure 1 callouts 8 and 9: the OFFLINE button at 419.3 mm across and 31.9 mm down, and the RESET pinhole at 427.7 mm and 35.6 mm, each legend under it. The OFFLINE button is a 6.0 mm part written for it, since no other library part is a small ring button.

chassis.note: Guide Table 4: 1.72 in (4.37 cm) high, 18.5 in (47 cm) deep or 20.43 in (51.89 cm) with the fan tray and power supply handles, 19 in (48.26 cm) wide, 22.7 lb (10.3 kg). The 19 in is the width with the front-mounting brackets (Table 22 says the brackets extend the chassis to 19 in), so it is not the body. Datasheet Table 5 gives 17.6 x 1.75 x 18.7 in (44.7 x 4.45 x 47.5 cm), and the specifications page 17.4 x 1.75 x 18 in (44.2 x 4.4 x 45.7 cm). The three disagree on every axis. The body width is the datasheet's 447.0 mm, since the guide's is the width with brackets; the height is the guide's 43.7 mm (the datasheet's 44.5 is the 1 U pitch) and the depth the guide's 18.5 in, 469.9 mm, the chassis without handles. See the gap named chassis-size.

colour.note: The median of bare patches on the photograph's face is #8d9096 and the lit lid #d4d4d7; the chassis colour is the face's, #8b8e94, a mid grey. The photograph is lit and these are its values, not a paint reference.

ears-and-kits.note: NOT MODELLED. The guide mounts the switch on four posts of a 19 in or an ETSI rack with two front-mounting brackets (16 screws), two rear-mounting brackets and, for ETSI, four ETSI brackets, all in the accessory box (Table 32); the brackets are flush with the faceplate in Figures 24 and 25. No rail or mounting kit has a part number, and the library holds no contract for the brackets, so chassis.ears and chassis.kits are left out and a gap says so.

esd.note: Figure 1 draws a hex-nut jack at the lower left, 13.0 mm across and 29.5 mm down, with the ESD mark beneath it. The guide's front panel callout list has no entry for it; the guide's text says to connect the strap "to the ESD point on the switch" and the rear (Figure 2, callout 2) has one as well.

fans-and-supplies.note: The three fan trays (JNP-FAN-1RU in the datasheet's ordering table, labelled AIR OUT) and the two power supplies are field-replaceable units in bays, each its own component; the empty supply slot takes the blank JNP-PWR-BLNK-1 (Table 3). The Routing Engine is built in on the baseboard and cannot be replaced (Routing Engine, page 5), so it is part of the chassis and not a bay. The fan in each supply is inside the supply. The supplies are juniper/ex4600-jpsu-650-ac-afo@1 and juniper/ex4600-jpsu-650-dc-afo@1, reused as they are: Table 2 names the EX9251's supplies "AC AFO 650W PSU" and JPSU-650W-DC-AFO, the AC supply's lamps AC, DC and ! and its C14 inlet are the EX9251's (Figures 14 and 17), and the DC supply's V-, V-, V+, V+ terminals, IN, OUT and ! lamps and ESD point are the EX9251's (Figure 17). The datasheet's spare part numbers for them are JNP-PWR650-AC and JNP-PWR650-DC. See the gap named psu-reuse.

gate-1.note: Guide Figures 1 and 3 are 1500 px wide rasters of the front and the DC rear, drawn flat. The rack outline of Figure 1, ears included, is 1444 x 135 px, an aspect of 10.70 against 482.6 / 44.45 = 10.86 for a 19 in 1 U plate (1.5 percent out), and the DC rear outline is 1445 x 134 px, 10.78 (0.7 percent out). So both are read as flat, at 2.992 px/mm across and 3.0 down. The body is placed centred in the outline: its left edge is 69.2 px in on the front and 68.3 px in on the rear, where the datasheet's 447.0 mm body leaves 17.8 mm of bracket on each side. The figure's own fold lines are 79 and 1398 px, which read 440.9 mm, 1.4 percent narrower than the datasheet; the datasheet is followed. Rows are taken from the figure's top outline at 145.7 px (front) so that the 43.7 mm body spans the 1 U outline. Every position read off these figures is estimated to about 0.7 mm: a pixel is 0.33 mm and the width scale is uncertain by the 1.5 percent above.

lamps.note: Figure 1 and Table 7: the lamps OK/FAIL, ONLINE, ALM, SSD1 and SSD0 in a row at 35.2 mm down, centred over their legends, 370.9, 382.3, 392.3, 401.0 and 409.0 mm across. Table 7 gives their colours (ONLINE green or red, OK/FAIL green or red, ALM red or yellow, the SSD lamps green). The figure's lamp rings are 4.7 mm; the lamp part is 2.0 mm.

lifecycle.note: Searched for an end-of-life notice. No Juniper bulletin was found. Two third-party trackers (endoflife.ai, parkplacetechnologies.com) give an end of service life of 2027-03-31 for the EX9251-8X4C, with no last order date; that is not a Juniper notice, so none is written as announced.

logo-zones.note: Figure 1 prints the maker's lockup at the upper left (6.0 to 28.7 mm across, 1.4 to 10.2 mm down) and a Junos OS mark at the right (423.2 to 439.7 mm, 4.8 to 10.8 mm). Neither is drawn: both are reserved as regions. The text EX9251 beside the left one is plain model text and is drawn.

mgmt-ports.note: Figure 1 callouts 2 and 3, 13 and 14: MGMT (the management Ethernet port, a 10/100/1000 autosensing RJ-45), BITS, CON (the RS-232 console) and ToD, all RJ-45 and 22 to 24 mm apart from 250.2 mm across. MGMT and BITS carry their latch step at the top and the lamps in the top corners, so they are drawn turned 180; CON and ToD carry their contacts at the top. The photograph shows the same four jacks, silver housings with the lamps of MGMT and BITS in the top corners. Table 7 and Figures 7 and 8: MGMT has a speed lamp and a link/activity lamp, BITS an activity lamp and a link lamp. The guide's text says the ToD port has a lamp (Table 36, step 4); no figure shows it, and it is not drawn (see the gap named tod-lamp).

port-lamps.note: Guide Figure 4 and Table 5: four lamps above each QSFP28 cage, LED0 (the 100G or 40G link, or the first 10G lane) to LED3. In Figure 4 they sit 4.0 mm above the cage, 4.0 mm apart, the first 3.7 mm in from the cage's left edge (8.16 px/mm on that figure's 155 px cage). Figures 5 and 6: each SFP+ column has four triangles in the band between its rows, down, up, down, up from the left; the lamp of the upper (even) port is the fourth, pointing up, and the lamp of the lower (odd) port the first, pointing down. The second and third are printed outlines. The triangles are at 1.8, 5.1, 8.8 and 11.8 mm from the column's left edge. The guide says each SFP+ port has one lamp.

port-numbering.note: Printed on the metal (Figures 1, 5 and 6): the QSFP28 ports are 0/0 to 0/3 under their cages, and the SFP+ ports 1/0 to 1/7 in four columns, each column printed with two legends, the upper port's above the lower's (1/0 over 1/1, 1/2 over 1/3, 1/4 over 1/5, 1/6 over 1/7) under the lower cage. Figures 5 and 6 say the upper cage of a column is the port with the even number and the lower the odd one. The ids are the printed label with a dash: port-0-0 to port-0-3 and port-1-0 to port-1-7. Table 2 names the PICs 4XQSFP28 (PIC slot 0) and 8XSFPP (PIC slot 1), which is the first digit of the printed label. The guide does not print the interface names, so none is written.

ports.note: Figure 1 at 2.992 px/mm: the four QSFP28 openings run 216 to 446 px, 76.9 mm, against 4 x 19.0 = 76.0 mm for the registry's qsfp-ganged pitch, so the block is centred on the figure's span at the registry pitch, its first cell at 49.75 mm. The four SFP+ columns run 466 to 640 px, 58.2 mm, the registry's own 4 x 14.25 + 1.2 = 58.2 mm for a 1 x 4 SFP+ bezel, so the block's first column starts at 133.2 mm. The GM/PTP cage centres at 174 px, 34.9 mm. Counts: callout 1 (four rate-selectable ports), callout 15 (eight SFP+ ports) and callout 16 (GM/PTP), all from Figure 1.

power.note: Guide Table 12: fully loaded switch 240 W typical at 25 C and 280 W maximum at 55 C. Tables 13 and 14 add the supply efficiency, 266 W and 311 W at 90 percent. Table 15 (AC): 100 to 240 VAC, 50 to 60 Hz, 3.2 A at 100 VAC and 1.37 A at 240 VAC, system input power 312 W. Table 17 (DC): -44 to -72 VDC, 20 A maximum at -44 VDC, system input power 331 W. The datasheet's Table 3 gives a maximum power draw of 300 W on AC and 312 W on DC, and Table 20 of the guide a maximum thermal output of 1705 BTU/hour (500 W); the datasheet says 1,275 BTU/hour (360 W). They are different scopes and the figures are kept as they are printed.

rear-layout.note: Figures 2 and 3 at 2.994 px/mm: a plate at the left with the protective earthing terminal (two tapped holes for 10-32 screws, 16 mm apart, 20.6 and 36.6 mm across) under the earth mark, and the ESD point at 61.1 mm; three fan slots numbered 0 to 2 on a 48.4 mm pitch, each preceded by a strip with its fan symbol, numeral and lamp; a blank plate of 73.5 x 39.8 mm; and two power supply slots numbered 0 and 1 at 318.9 and 381.6 mm. The strip's lamps are the fan tray status lamps of Figure 12 and Table 8.

rear-plate.note: Figures 2 and 3 both draw a plain rectangular plate between the third fan tray and the first supply, 238.7 to 312.2 mm across. The guide does not name it. It is drawn as plain metal and carries no part.

row-pitch.note: The SFP+ block is two cages stacked with a lamp band between them: the top cage's front edge at 173 px and the bottom cage's at 223 px, 16.7 mm apart, against the registry's 15.0 mm belly-to-belly pitch, which the registry marks as measured off another cage. The extra 1.7 mm is the band of triangles. 16.7 mm is written, read off Figure 1 and Figure 5.

sources.note: Juniper EX9251 Switch Hardware Guide, published 2022-11-30, 217 pages (Juniper Networks, copyright 2022), https://www.juniper.net/documentation/us/en/hardware/ex9251/ex9251.pdf: Table 1 (the models), Table 2 (the CLI names), Tables 3 and 4 (spare parts and the chassis), the front panel (Figure 1), the rear panels (Figures 2 and 3), the lamps (Figures 4 to 8, Tables 5 to 7), the cooling system (Figures 9 to 12, Table 8), the power system (Figures 13 to 17, Tables 9 to 18) and the environmental table (Table 20). EX9250 Ethernet Switch Datasheet, 1000632-006-EN, Sep 2021 (PDF produced 2022-07-27): the chassis table (Table 5) and the ordering table. The datasheet's own address now redirects to a page on the hpe.com site, which did not answer; the PDF was read from the Internet Archive's capture of Juniper's address (https://web.archive.org/web/20240111201612/https://www.juniper.net/content/dam/www/assets/datasheets/us/en/switches/ex9250-ethernet-switch-datasheet.pdf). Juniper's EX9250 specifications page (https://www.juniper.net/us/en/products/switches/ex-series/ex9250-core-and-aggregation-switches/specs.html) for the third set of dimensions, and Juniper's image library photograph ex9250-11 (https://juniper-prod.scene7.com/is/image/junipernetworks/ex9250-11), a three-quarter view of the EX9251 front, 3000 x 153 px, used for the colour and to confirm the cages, jacks and lamps. Terms: the documents and the photograph are Juniper's, read here for facts only, and nothing of them is copied into the library. No held intake folder, Visio stencil or 3D model was reachable from this work (the intake folders named in the issue do not exist for this account), so the public documents above are the only sources.

stack-orientation.note: Figure 1 and Figure 5 draw the latch tongue at the foot of each upper SFP+ cage and at the top of each lower one, so both lips face the band between the rows: the upper cage upright and the lower one turned 180, the library's stack convention.

usb-timing.note: Figure 1: the USB port is vertical, 335.6 mm across, with the USB mark beneath it; two columns of SMB connectors follow, 10MHz at 350.3 mm and 1PPS at 360.0 mm, the upper row IN (23.9 mm down) and the lower row OUT (31.9 mm down), each legend under its row. The guide (Connecting 1-PPS and 10-MHz Timing Devices) calls them SMB connectors.

vents.note: Figure 1 and the photograph show the face perforated with hexagonal holes everywhere the parts are not. Four plain rectangles in the clear areas are declared as vents (above the QSFP28 block, between the SFP+ block and the MGMT jack, above the MGMT to USB group, and right of the timing connectors) and a small one at the left. They are not the holes one by one.

bottom.empty: Not drawn by any source held. The guide's figures show no underside.

placements.description: the PTP grandmaster clock port, GM/PTP; the guide says support for it is not available in this release (Figure 1, callout 16)
the management Ethernet port, 10/100/1000 autosensing RJ-45, with a speed lamp and a link/activity lamp (Figure 1, callout 2; Figure 7, Table 7)
the BITS port, the building-integrated timing supply clock interface (Figure 1, callout 3; Figure 8)
Table 7 - green: no loss, BITS is in the locked state; unlit: loss of signal or loss of line
Table 7 - amber: loss of signal or loss of line; unlit: no loss
the console port, RS-232 over an RJ-45 (Figure 1, callout 14; Table 28)
the time of day port, ToD (Figure 1, callout 13; Table 36)
Table 7 - green steady: the switch is functioning normally; red blinking: the switch has failed; unlit: not powered on
Table 7 - green steady: Junos OS and Linux are loaded; green blinking: starting Junos OS; red steady: Linux loaded; red blinking: starting Linux; unlit: offline
Table 7 - red steady: major alarm; red blinking: a major and a minor alarm; yellow steady: minor alarm; unlit: no alarm
Table 7 - green blinking: SSD1 is being accessed; unlit: not active
Table 7 - green blinking: SSD0 is being accessed; unlit: not active
turns the switch online or offline, or powers it on or off (Figure 1, callout 8)

left.empty: Not drawn by any source held. The guide draws the brackets on the side wall in three-quarter view only, with no scale from which a hole could be placed.

placements.description: Table 8 - green blinking: hardware initialised, software pending; green steady: functioning normally; red: faulty; unlit: not present

right.empty: Not drawn by any source held. No figure shows the right wall flat.

top.empty: Not drawn by any source held. The guide shows no figure of the lid except the location of the serial number label (Figure 63), and the photograph is a three-quarter view of the front.
